messages.subject: plotDensity(rs)
parts:
I get two very different plots when I do A or B below.

"A" gives me two peaks, one centered around 0, the other centered
around 7. The one centered around 7 is about 3 times as tall as the
one around 0.

"B" gives me on peak around 0.

Any clues?

A:
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
rs = calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)
plotDensity(rs, ylim=c(0,1.2), main="residuals")

B:
cellInd = getCellIndices(cdf);
rs.vec = getData(rs, indices=unlist(cellInd), field="intensities");
plot(density(log2(rs.vec$intensities)))

victoria

messages.author: 544a2f5526cc67ef
messages.subject: Re: plotDensity(rs)
parts:

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: plotDensity(rs)
parts:
Hi Victoria,

As you correctly point out, "A" is trying to plot everything (actually, half
the probes; plotDensity.AffymetrixCelSet() takes a random subset of 1/2 the
probes by default), while "B" is taking just the subset you specify. Note
that you could also do

plotDensity(rs, subset=unlist(cellInd))

for "B".

Cheers,

Ken
